body:
Hmm, `Content-Type: application/json` is definitely not added by `quarkus-oidc`.

@geoand @FroMage hey, are you aware of `RestEasy Reactive` or Vert.x route filter setting this content type if no content type is set ?
I know JSON is supported by default by Resteasy Reactive

rename.from: Challenge response has JSON content type without body
rename.to: OIDC Challenge response has JSON content type without body

body:
Yeah, it's used as the default in RR when a Resource method returns a POJO.
It would be nice to have a reproducer here in order to investigate exactly what's going on.
@geoand I'll do a quick check with one of the local tests a bit later

Activating brain. I'll keep working on the reproducer...

EDIT: I've woken up and fixed the reproducer :roll_eyes:

Thanks @Adelrisk. I also did an independent test not even related to OIDC as such but to the authorization failure,

@geoand, FYI, if you update [this test](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/tree/main/integration-tests/oidc-client-reactive), specifically, [ProtectedResource#userNameReactive](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/integration-tests/oidc-client-reactive/src/main/java/io/quarkus/it/keycloak/ProtectedResource.java#L32) to have some random value in `@RolesAllowed` and then add
```
quarkus.rest-client.logging.scope=request-response
quarkus.rest-client.logging.body-limit=50
quarkus.log.category."org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.client.logging".level=DEBUG
```
to `application.properties` and run the test as `mvn clean install -Dstart-containers -Dtest-containers > out.txt` and then search for `Response:`, you'll see: 
```
2023-02-15 19:08:17,450 DEBUG [org.jbo.res.rea.cli.log.DefaultClientLogger] (vert.x-eventloop-thread-4) Response: GET http://localhost:8081/protected/userNameReactive, Status[403 Forbidden], Headers[Content-Type=text/plain;charset=UTF-8 content-length=0], Body:
``` 

I guess the technical problem is, that when `Content-Type` is set in the response, it is not known yet if the actual body will be available ? If it is somehow possible to check then it would be simplest. Alternatively, set `Content-Type` only if it is `HTTP 200`, but there is a small risk of even `403` or `401` returning some custom data...
That's the question... I'd have to check and see

issue.title: Ensure no content-type header is sent when no HTTP body exists
